source.title: Kronecker Factorization Improves Efficiency and Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Vadim Kurochkin; Yaroslav Aksenov; Daniil Laptev; Daniil Gavrilov; Nikita Balagansky

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and figure layouts are flattened, but the relevant text and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies an SAE feature-learning and interpretability approach to activations from pretrained language models and reports results about learned features. It does not reproduce or directly test the Toy Models of Superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE interpretability and feature-correlation results that bear on indirect evidence for interpretable SAE features in language models. It does not test whether sparse features exceeding dimensionality are stored as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, nor does it test neuron-level capacity competition or canonicality. Reconstruction, FLOP, and compatibility results are not included because they do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE architecture paper. It uses SAEs as a tool on Gemma-2-2B and Qwen2.5-1.5B residual streams and reports how its own KronSAE compares with TopK, Matryoshka and Switch SAEs on explained variance, FLOPs, auto-interpretability, absorption and correlation recovery. It never tests whether the models contain recoverable sparse features, or any other version. The interpretability gain in R1 is a comparison of methods, not evidence on V4. The toy experiment borrows the Elhage et al. autoencoder only as a source of synthetic hidden states for a correlation-recovery sanity check. It reports no superposition geometry, phase transition or capacity allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that KronSAE matches TopK on the EV–FLOPs frontier with cheaper encoders, gives more interpretable and specific latents, captures correlated feature structure better, and reduces absorption. They call the toy experiment a sanity check of the inductive bias.
record.recipe_differences: This is a new Kronecker-factorized SAE encoder with an AND-like interaction, trained to learn compositional SAE latents. It does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported geometry and trade-offs vary with KronSAE head and pre-latent dimensions (h, m, n); the authors state that absorption and interpretability trade-offs also vary with sparsity and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: KronSAE latents on Gemma-2-2B layer 12 get higher detection and fuzzing scores and lower token entropy than TopK SAE latents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compositional (Kronecker-factorized) SAE encoders yield more interpretable, more specific latents than flat TopK SAEs.

fits_no_version.finding: Correlated features from a flat TopK SAE map to KronSAE features in common heads far more often than chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KronSAE heads group correlated SAE features into shared compositional subspaces.

fits_no_version.finding: KronSAE features correlate more within a head than across heads, and within-head correlations increase after training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The factorized SAE architecture induces and learns head-local correlation structure.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic block-correlated data, KronSAE gets a higher RV coefficient against the target than TopK SAE, both in the displayed setup and across 8 covariance setups.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KronSAE recovers imposed block-structured feature correlations better than a flat TopK SAE in synthetic setups.

fits_no_version.finding: A selected Gemma example shows a polysemous base pre-latent and more specific composed post-latents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In KronSAE, AND-like composition makes post-latents narrower than their pre-latents.

fits_no_version.finding: KronSAE variants reduce mean absorption and full absorption while keeping a similar feature-splitting rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KronSAE reduces SAE feature absorption without increasing feature splitting in the tested Gemma setup.

record.problems: The authors state that evaluation is limited to mid-sized transformer models and that the toy experiment is primarily a sanity check; real-world correlation structure may differ. The interpretability results rely on an automated LLM-based pipeline. Several relevant figure results have no exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; all selected claim-relevant results are included.

untested.parts: All of it. The Elhage-style autoencoder is used only to generate synthetic hidden states; no superposition geometry, sparsity transition or orthogonality is measured.
All of it. The authors attribute polysemantic pre-latents to reduced encoder capacity by design, but this is a hypothesis about their own architecture, not about model neurons.
All of it. No test of whether LLM activations contain sparse features recoverable by an SAE, beyond SAE-vs-SAE comparisons.
All of it. No stability, completeness or canonicality tests across runs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed: R1 is a comparison of the study's own method with a baseline, not a measurement of whether models contain SAE-recoverable features. Appendix G mentions decoder-atom clustering geometry and attributes pre-latent polysemanticity to capacity, but both concern the SAE's own architecture, not the model's representation.

versions.untested_parts: No test of superposition, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or the predicted regular geometry of overcomplete sparse features.

The paper discusses polysemantic SAE pre-latents, but does not test whether neurons become polysemantic because features compete for capacity, or whether importance determines which features receive dedicated dimensions.

No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure. The paper's qualitative examples concern deliberately factorized SAE pre-latents, not naturally occurring neuron polysemanticity.

Tests automated interpretability of SAE latents on language-model activations, but not whether features are distributed across many neurons or whether SAE latents are ground-truth features of the model.
No assessment of whether SAE features are complete, stable across runs, or canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features as the underlying units of superposition.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared automated interpretation scores for TopK SAE and KronSAE latents.
rows.measure: Automated interpretability scores (detection and fuzzing); feature specificity properties are also compared.
rows.value: The text states that KronSAE features have higher interpretability scores and are more specific; exact score values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: This is indirect evidence that an SAE can produce interpretable latents from model activations; the study does not verify those latents against ground-truth model features.
rows.check: This row compares the study's own method (KronSAE) with a TopK baseline. Relative auto-interpretability scores do not measure whether the LLM contains sparse features an SAE recovers, so the row should not be linked to V4. It is better treated as a method-comparison row with no version.

rows.subject: TopK SAE and KronSAE (underlying model not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Mapped correlated TopK features to their top-r correlated KronSAE features and measured whether matches shared a head.
rows.measure: Fraction of correlated TopK feature pairs with at least one pair of mapped KronSAE features in the same head.
rows.value: The text states that all observations are far above chance; exact values are figure-only.
rows.note: This measures head-wise grouping of correlated SAE features, not superposition geometry.

rows.subject: Randomly initialized KronSAE

rows.measure: Mean Pearson correlation within a head versus between heads.
rows.baseline: Between-head correlations; exact values are figure-only.
rows.value: Figure-only; the text reports higher correlations within a head than between heads.
rows.note: This is a random-initialization comparison for the head-wise correlation analysis.

rows.subject: Trained KronSAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean feature correlations within heads and across heads.
rows.measure: Mean Pearson correlation within a head versus between heads.
rows.baseline: Randomly initialized KronSAE; exact values are figure-only.
rows.value: Figure-only; the text reports that within-head correlations increase further after training and that correlations across heads are also learned.
rows.note: The result concerns learned correlation structure, not the overlap or orthogonality of superposed features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B SAE features, head 23
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively interpreted a base pre-latent and its compositions with extension pre-latents.
rows.measure: Interpretations and interpretation scores for the pre-latent and composed post-latents.
rows.value: The base is described as having multiple detectable sub-semantics; its compositions are described as narrower or more specific. Scores in Table 1 range from 0.66 to 0.93.
rows.note: This is a selected qualitative example of polysemous SAE pre-latents and more specific compositions, not a test of neuron polysemanticity.

reader_labels.reason: The study reports higher automated interpretability scores for KronSAE latents than for TopK SAE latents, providing indirect evidence that an SAE can yield interpretable features from language-model activations (R1).
